chunks: Al-Tatari narrated from Ali ibn Ribat from Ya'qub ibn Salim from Abdullah who said:
I asked him about a man who fears ritual impurity (janabah) during travel or the cold; should he hasten the night prayer and the witr prayer at the beginning of the night? He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةَ: Ritual impurity requiring a full body bath (ghusl)
key_terms.وَالْوَتْرَ: And the witr prayer (odd-numbered prayer concluding night prayers)

ai.seo_question: When should one perform night prayer if fearing cold or ritual impurity?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Imam confirms that fear of *janabah* (ritual impurity) or cold during travel serves as a valid legal excuse (*'udhr*) to advance the voluntary night prayer (*Salat al-Layl*) and *Witr* to the early part of the night. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of balancing spiritual diligence with practical ease, allowing believers to secure their voluntary acts of worship before potential impediments arise, thereby preserving the reward without incurring hardship.
